messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

You will be given a piece of text and a list of relational triples in the format of [Subject, Relation, Object] extracted from the text. For each relation present in the triples, your task is to write a description to express the meaning of the relation.

Here are some examples:
Example 1:
Text: Lipitor (atorvastatin) belongs to a group of drugs called statins. Lipitor is used together with diet to lower blood levels of "bad" cholesterol (LDL) and to reduce the risk of stroke and heart attack.
Triples: [["Lipitor", "has generic name", "atorvastatin"], ["Lipitor", "belongs to drug class", "statins"], ["Lipitor", "treats", "high LDL cholesterol"], ["Lipitor", "reduces risk of", "stroke"]]
Relations: ["has generic name", "belongs to drug class", "treats", "reduces risk of"]
Answer:
has generic name: The subject drug is known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.
belongs to drug class: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.
reduces risk of: The subject drug is used to lower the risk of the medical event or condition specified by the object entity.

Example 2:
Text: You should not use metformin if you have severe kidney disease. Tell your doctor if you have ever had liver disease. Metformin may cause lactic acidosis, a serious condition. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking metformin.
Triples: [["metformin", "contraindicated in", "severe kidney disease"], ["metformin", "use with caution in", "liver disease"], ["metformin", "has serious side effect", "lactic acidosis"], ["metformin", "should be avoided with", "alcohol"]]
Relations: ["contraindicated in", "use with caution in", "has serious side effect", "should be avoided with"]
Answer:
contraindicated in: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
use with caution in: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
has serious side effect: The subject drug may cause the serious or dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity.
should be avoided with: Patients taking the subject drug should avoid the substance or activity specified by the object entity.

Example 3:
Text: Amlodipine is available as oral tablets in strengths of 2.5 mg, 5 mg, and 10 mg. Overdose symptoms may include rapid heartbeats and fainting. Norvasc is made by Pfizer.
Triples: [["amlodipine", "has dosage form", "oral tablet"], ["amlodipine", "has strength", "2.5 mg"], ["amlodipine", "has overdose symptom", "fainting"], ["Norvasc", "manufactured by", "Pfizer"]]
Relations: ["has dosage form", "has strength", "has overdose symptom", "manufactured by"]
Answer:
has dosage form: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
has strength: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
has overdose symptom: An overdose of the subject drug may cause the symptom specified by the object entity.
manufactured by: The subject drug is manufactured or marketed by the company specified by the object entity.

Now please write relation descriptions given the following text and triples. Note that the description needs to be general and can be used to describe relations between other entities as well. Pay attention to the order of subject and object entities. Write exactly one line per relation in the form "relation: description" and nothing else.
Text: Both brands have been discontinued in the United States.
Hydroxyzine is now available as a generic medicine.
Is hydroxyzine pamoate stronger or longer lasting than hydroxyzine hydrochloride?
:
No.
You may read that hydroxyzine pamoate works better for anxiety.
You may read that hydroxyzine pamoate lasts longer.
You may read that hydroxyzine pamoate reaches the brain more effectively than hydroxyzine hydrochloride.
FDA-approved labeling does not support this.
Labeling for both salt forms states that hydroxyzine's effects are usually noticed within 15 to 30 minutes.
The effects are noticed after a dose taken by mouth.
Both are approved for the same three uses.
Both carry the same doses.
The doses are 50 to 100 mg four times a day for anxiety in adults.
The doses are 25 mg three or four times a day for itching.
No FDA labeling describes a difference in how strongly or how long either form works.
The doses match.
This is because hydroxyzine pamoate capsules are labeled by their hydroxyzine hydrochloride equivalent.
Triples: [["hydroxyzine hydrochloride", "has brand name", "hydroxyzine"], ["hydroxyzine pamoate", "has brand name", "hydroxyzine"], ["hydroxyzine hydrochloride", "has discontinued status", "United States"], ["hydroxyzine pamoate", "has discontinued status", "United States"], ["hydroxyzine", "available as", "generic medicine"], ["hydroxyzine pamoate", "has claim", "stronger or longer lasting than hydroxyzine hydrochloride"], ["hydroxyzine pamoate", "has claim", "works better for anxiety"], ["hydroxyzine pamoate", "has claim", "lasts longer"], ["hydroxyzine pamoate", "has claim", "reaches the brain more effectively than hydroxyzine hydrochloride"], ["FDA-approved labeling", "does not support", "hydroxyzine pamoate stronger or longer lasting than hydroxyzine hydrochloride"], ["hydroxyzine", "has effect onset time", "15 to 30 minutes"], ["hydroxyzine", "has administration route", "oral"], ["hydroxyzine hydrochloride", "approved for use", "anxiety"], ["hydroxyzine pamoate", "approved for use", "anxiety"], ["hydroxyzine hydrochloride", "approved for use", "itching"], ["hydroxyzine pamoate", "approved for use", "itching"], ["hydroxyzine hydrochloride", "has recommended dose", "50 to 100 mg four times a day for anxiety in adults"], ["hydroxyzine pamoate", "has recommended dose", "50 to 100 mg four times a day for anxiety in adults"], ["hydroxyzine hydrochloride", "has recommended dose", "25 mg three or four times a day for itching"], ["hydroxyzine pamoate", "has recommended dose", "25 mg three or four times a day for itching"], ["FDA labeling", "does not describe difference in", "strength or duration of effect between hydroxyzine hydrochloride and hydroxyzine pamoate"], ["hydroxyzine hydrochloride", "has dose equivalence", "hydroxyzine pamoate capsules"], ["hydroxyzine pamoate capsules", "labeled by", "hydroxyzine hydrochloride equivalent"]]
Relations: ["approved for use", "available as", "does not describe difference in", "does not support", "has administration route", "has brand name", "has claim", "has discontinued status", "has dose equivalence", "has effect onset time", "has recommended dose", "labeled by"]
Answer:

completion:
approved for use: The subject drug is approved by regulatory authorities for the medical condition or indication specified by the object entity.  
available as: The subject drug is available in the form or formulation specified by the object entity.  
does not describe difference in: The subject entity does not describe a difference in the characteristic specified by the object entity between two drugs or forms.  
does not support: The subject entity does not support or endorse the claim specified by the object entity.  
has administration route: The subject drug is administered via the route specified by the object entity.  
has brand name: The subject drug is marketed under the brand name specified by the object entity.  
has claim: The subject drug is associated with the claim or assertion specified by the object entity.  
has discontinued status: The subject drug is no longer available or has been discontinued in the region or country specified by the object entity.  
has dose equivalence: The subject drug is considered equivalent in dose to the drug specified by the object entity.  
has effect onset time: The subject drug begins to take effect within the time frame specified by the object entity.  
has recommended dose: The subject drug is prescribed at the dose specified by the object entity for a particular condition or use.  
labeled by: The subject drug is labeled or measured based on the equivalent dose or form specified by the object entity.
